subject: Financial Accounting
title: Reconciliations and Control Accounts
outline: Purpose of the bank statement and the cash book
Causes of disagreement: unpresented cheques, uncredited lodgements, bank charges
Updating the cash book and preparing the bank reconciliation statement
Sales ledger and purchases ledger control accounts
Sources of entries in control accounts and set-off (contra) entries
Types of errors and their correction through the journal
The suspense account and its effect on net profit

modules.title: Bank Reconciliation Statement
modules.html:
1. Why the Two Records Differ

  1. Unpresented cheques - cheques drawn and entered in the cash book but not yet presented for payment.
  2. Uncredited lodgements - cheques paid in but not yet cleared by the bank.
  3. Bank charges, commission and interest on overdraft - known only from the statement.
  4. Direct credits - standing orders received, dividends and customer transfers.
  5. Standing orders and direct debits paid by the bank.
  6. Dishonoured cheques returned unpaid.
  7. Errors by either the cashier or the bank.

2. Two-Stage Procedure

Stage 1 - Update the cash book for items the business did not know about: add direct credits and interest received; deduct bank charges, standing orders, direct debits and dishonoured cheques. This gives the adjusted (corrected) cash book balance.

Stage 2 - Prepare the reconciliation statement:

Bank Reconciliation Statement as at 31 DecemberN
Balance as per adjusted cash book418,000
Add unpresented cheques96,000
Less uncredited lodgements(64,000)
Balance as per bank statement450,000

Starting instead from the bank statement, the signs reverse: deduct unpresented cheques and add uncredited lodgements. An overdraft is a credit balance in the bank statement and a credit balance in the cash book; the same logic applies but with negative figures.

3. Importance

  • Detects errors and possible fraud by the cashier.
  • Reveals stale and dishonoured cheques.
  • Confirms the true bank figure for the balance sheet.

examples.q: Cash book balance (debit) N540,000. Bank charges N12,000 and a standing order of N38,000 had not been entered; a customer paid N75,000 directly into the bank. Unpresented cheques were N120,000 and uncredited lodgements N90,000. Prepare the reconciliation.
examples.a: Adjusted cash book = 540,000 - 12,000 - 38,000 + 75,000 = N565,000. Reconciliation: adjusted cash book N565,000 + unpresented cheques N120,000 - uncredited lodgements N90,000 = balance per bank statement N595,000. The balance sheet shows the adjusted figure of N565,000.

examples.q: Why is a cheque drawn but not yet presented added to the cash book balance when reconciling to the bank statement?
examples.a: The business has already credited (reduced) its cash book for the payment, but the bank has not yet debited the account because the payee has not presented the cheque. The bank's balance is therefore higher by that amount, so the cheque is added back to the adjusted cash book balance to arrive at the bank statement balance.

modules.title: Control Accounts
modules.html:
1. Purpose

A control (total) account is a summary account whose balance should equal the total of the individual balances in the corresponding subsidiary ledger. It locates errors quickly, permits division of labour, provides internal check against fraud, and enables debtors and creditors totals to be obtained without listing every account.

2. Sales Ledger (Debtors) Control Account

Debit sideCredit side
Opening debtors balance b/d
Credit sales
Dishonoured cheques
Interest charged to customers
Refunds to customers
Bad debts previously written off and now reinstated		Cash and cheques received
Discount allowed
Returns inwards
Bad debts written off
Set-off / contra to purchases ledger
Closing balance c/d

3. Purchases Ledger (Creditors) Control Account

Debit sideCredit side
Payments to suppliers
Discount received
Returns outwards
Set-off / contra
Closing balance c/d		Opening creditors balance b/d
Credit purchases
Interest charged by suppliers

Sources of the figures are the totals of the books of original entry, not the individual ledger accounts - this independence is what makes the control account a genuine check.

4. Set-off (Contra) Entries

Where the same person is both a debtor and a creditor, the smaller balance may be set against the larger: Dr Purchases Ledger Control, Cr Sales Ledger Control.

examples.q: Prepare a debtors control account: opening debtors N860,000; credit sales N4,200,000; cash received N3,600,000; discount allowed N90,000; returns inwards N140,000; bad debts written off N60,000; set-off N40,000. Find the closing debtors.
The creditors control account shows N1,480,000 but the list of creditors totals N1,510,000. Give two possible reasons.
examples.a: (i) A credit purchase of N30,000 may have been posted to the supplier's personal account but omitted from the purchases day book total used in the control account. (ii) A supplier's account may have been overcast by N30,000, or discount received of N30,000 entered in the control account but not in the personal account. Each is investigated and the appropriate record corrected so that the two figures agree.

modules.title: Correction of Errors and the Suspense Account
modules.html:
1. Correcting Errors Not Affecting the Trial Balance

These are corrected by a simple journal entry between two accounts, with no suspense account involved. Example: a sale to Ojo posted to Ojoo - Dr Ojo, Cr Ojoo.

2. Correcting Errors Affecting the Trial Balance

Each correction involves the Suspense Account on one side. When all errors have been corrected, the suspense account closes automatically.

ErrorCorrecting entry
Sales account undercast by N20,000Dr Suspense N20,000, Cr Sales N20,000
Discount received N9,000 not posted to the nominal ledgerDr Suspense N9,000, Cr Discount Received N9,000
Rent of N15,000 debited twiceDr Suspense N15,000, Cr Rent N15,000
Cash N30,000 from a debtor debited to cash but not credited to the debtorDr Suspense N30,000, Cr Debtor N30,000

3. Effect on Net Profit

Only errors touching nominal accounts (income and expense) change profit. Prepare a statement of corrected net profit:

Statement of Corrected Net ProfitN
Net profit as per draft accounts1,450,000
Add: Sales undercast20,000
Add: Discount received omitted9,000
Add: Rent debited twice15,000
Corrected net profit1,494,000

Errors involving only balance sheet items (e.g. the unposted debtor receipt) clear the suspense account but leave profit unchanged.

examples.q: A trial balance had a credit difference of N44,000 placed in suspense. Later it was found that the purchases account had been overcast by N44,000. Give the journal entry and the effect on profit.
examples.a: Dr Purchases? No - purchases were overstated, so we reduce them: Dr Suspense N44,000, Cr Purchases N44,000. Because purchases were overstated, cost of goods sold was too high and profit too low; correcting it increases net profit by N44,000, and the suspense account is cleared.

examples.q: Motor repairs of N250,000 were debited to the Motor Vehicles Account. Correct the error and state its effect.
examples.a: This is an error of principle; the trial balance still agreed. Correction: Dr Motor Repairs (expense) N250,000, Cr Motor Vehicles N250,000. Effect: net profit was overstated by N250,000 (before depreciation) and fixed assets were overstated by the same amount; after correction both are reduced.

modules.title: Purpose of the bank statement and the cash book
modules.html:
Purpose of the bank statement and the cash book is a key part of Reconciliations and Control Accounts (SSS 2, Financial Accounting). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Why the Two Records Differ Unpresented cheques - cheques drawn and entered in the cash book but not yet presented for payment.
  • Uncredited lodgements - cheques paid in but not yet cleared by the bank.
  • Bank charges, commission and interest on overdraft - known only from the statement.
  • Standing orders and direct debits paid by the bank.
  • Errors by either the cashier or the bank.

Worked example

Q: An unpresented cheque is one that has been:
A: Drawn but not yet paid by the bank — It has been entered in the cash book but not yet presented to the bank for payment.

Q: Bank charges appearing only on the bank statement should be:
A: Entered on the credit side of the cash book — Bank charges reduce the bank balance, so they are credited (entered on the payments side) in the cash book.

examples.q: An unpresented cheque is one that has been:
examples.a: Drawn but not yet paid by the bank — It has been entered in the cash book but not yet presented to the bank for payment.

examples.q: Bank charges appearing only on the bank statement should be:
examples.a: Entered on the credit side of the cash book — Bank charges reduce the bank balance, so they are credited (entered on the payments side) in the cash book.

modules.title: Sales ledger and purchases ledger control accounts
modules.html:
Sales ledger and purchases ledger control accounts is a key part of Reconciliations and Control Accounts (SSS 2, Financial Accounting). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Purpose A control (total) account is a summary account whose balance should equal the total of the individual balances in the corresponding subsidiary ledger.
  • Sales Ledger (Debtors) Control Account Debit side Credit side Opening debtors balance b/d Credit sales Dishonoured cheques Interest charged to customers Refunds to customers Bad debts previously written off and now reinstated Cash and cheques received Discount allowed Returns inwards Bad debts written off Set-off / contra to purchases ledger Closing balance c/d 3.
  • Purchases Ledger (Creditors) Control Account Debit side Credit side Payments to suppliers Discount received Returns outwards Set-off / contra Closing balance c/d Opening creditors balance b/d Credit purchases Interest charged by suppliers Sources of the figures are the totals of the books of original entry, not the individual ledger accounts - this independence is what makes the control account a genuine check.
  • Set-off (Contra) Entries Where the same person is both a debtor and a creditor, the smaller balance may be set against the larger: Dr Purchases Ledger Control, Cr Sales Ledger Control.
  • Correcting Errors Not Affecting the Trial Balance These are corrected by a simple journal entry between two accounts, with no suspense account involved.

Worked example

Q: Which item is credited in the sales ledger control account?
A: Discount allowed — Discount allowed reduces the amount receivable and appears on the credit side of the debtors control account.

Q: Credit purchases are posted to the creditors control account from the:
A: Purchases day book total — Control accounts take totals from the books of original entry, keeping them independent of the personal ledger.

examples.q: Which item is credited in the sales ledger control account?
examples.a: Discount allowed — Discount allowed reduces the amount receivable and appears on the credit side of the debtors control account.

examples.q: Credit purchases are posted to the creditors control account from the:
examples.a: Purchases day book total — Control accounts take totals from the books of original entry, keeping them independent of the personal ledger.

quiz.q: An unpresented cheque is one that has been:
options: Drawn but not yet paid by the bank
quiz.solution: It has been entered in the cash book but not yet presented to the bank for payment.

quiz.q: Bank charges appearing only on the bank statement should be:
options: Entered on the credit side of the cash book
quiz.solution: Bank charges reduce the bank balance, so they are credited (entered on the payments side) in the cash book.

quiz.q: Cash book N300,000 debit; unpresented cheques N80,000; uncredited lodgements N50,000. Bank statement balance is:
Which item is credited in the sales ledger control account?
quiz.solution: Discount allowed reduces the amount receivable and appears on the credit side of the debtors control account.

quiz.q: Credit purchases are posted to the creditors control account from the:
quiz.solution: Control accounts take totals from the books of original entry, keeping them independent of the personal ledger.

quiz.q: A set-off entry is:
options: Dr Sales Ledger Control, Cr Purchases Ledger Control
Dr Purchases Ledger Control, Cr Sales Ledger Control
quiz.solution: Where a person is both debtor and creditor, the amount is transferred by debiting the creditors control and crediting the debtors control.

quiz.q: Opening debtors N500,000; credit sales N2,000,000; receipts N1,700,000; returns inwards N60,000. Closing debtors are:
The main purpose of a control account is to:
options: Provide a check on the subsidiary ledger
quiz.solution: It provides an arithmetical check and helps locate errors within the sales or purchases ledger.

quiz.q: A suspense account with a credit balance means the trial balance had:
quiz.solution: A credit entry in suspense is needed to balance an excess of debits, so the debit total was larger.

quiz.q: Which error is corrected without using a suspense account?
quiz.solution: An error of commission has equal debit and credit, so the trial balance agreed and no suspense entry is needed.

quiz.q: A dishonoured cheque previously received from a debtor is entered in the debtors control account on the:
quiz.solution: The debt is reinstated, so the debtors control account is debited again.

quiz.q: Discount received appears in the creditors control account on the:
quiz.solution: Discount received reduces the amount payable and is therefore debited in the creditors control account.

quiz.q: Direct credit from a customer into the bank should be:
quiz.solution: It increases the bank balance and is therefore debited (receipts side) when updating the cash book.

quiz.q: Correction of an undercast in the sales account will:
quiz.solution: Sales were understated, so correcting the undercast increases revenue and therefore net profit.

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT appear in the debtors control account?
quiz.solution: Cash sales never create a debtor and so are excluded from the sales ledger control account.

quiz.q: A bank overdraft shown in the cash book is:
quiz.solution: An overdraft means more has been paid out than is available, giving a credit balance in the cash book and a current liability in the balance sheet.

quiz.q: Contra entries in Control Accounts happen when?
options: A person is both debtor and creditor
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: A person is both debtor and creditor.

quiz.q: The Purchases Ledger Control Account is used to check the accuracy of the _____.
quiz.solution: The Purchases Ledger Control Account (or Creditors Control) summarizes all transactions in the individual creditors' accounts.

quiz.q: The Sales Ledger Control Account is also known as _____.
quiz.solution: The Sales Ledger Control Account summarizes all transactions related to credit customers (debtors) to check the accuracy of the individual ledger accounts.

quiz.q: Sales Ledger Control Account is also called?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Total Debtors Account.

quiz.q: Purchases Ledger Control Account is also called?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Total Creditors Account.

quiz.q: A Control Account is used to?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Check errors in ledgers.

quiz.q: A Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared by the _____.
quiz.solution: The business prepares the Bank Reconciliation Statement to identify discrepancies between its Cash Book (Bank column) and the Bank Statement provided by the bank.

quiz.q: A Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared to _____.
options: Know the profit for the year
Reconcile the Cash Book and Bank Statement balances
quiz.solution: Discrepancies often exist between a business's Cash Book records and the Bank's Statement due to timing differences or errors; the statement aligns both.

quiz.q: Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared to reconcile:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Cash book and Bank statement.

quiz.q: A Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: The Customer (Business).

quiz.q: The process of transferring entries from a journal to a ledger is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Posting.

quiz.q: The rule for Real Accounts is?
options: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out.

quiz.q: Nominal Accounts deal with?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Expenses and Income.

quiz.q: Personal Accounts are accounts of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Persons and Firms.

quiz.q: Fixed Capital Accounts stay the same unless?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: More capital is introduced.

quiz.q: Current Accounts of partners record?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Profits, drawings, and interest.

quiz.q: Branch Accounts are for?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Businesses with multiple locations.

quiz.q: Which is an External User of accounts?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Investors.

quiz.q: "Window Dressing" in accounts is?
options: Making accounts look better than they are
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Making accounts look better than they are.

quiz.q: The process of transferring entries from the journals to the ledger is known as _____.
quiz.solution: Posting is the technical term for transferring data from the books of original entry (journals) to the principal book (ledger).

quiz.q: The systematic record of the cash and bank transactions of a business is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Cash Book serves as both a book of original entry and a ledger account for cash and bank balances.

quiz.q: A suspense account is used to _____.
quiz.solution: When a Trial Balance fails to agree, the difference is temporarily placed in a Suspense Account until the errors are located and corrected.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a book of prime entry AND a ledger?
quiz.solution: The Cash Book is unique because it serves both as the initial record of transactions and as the final T-account for cash and bank.

quiz.q: Sales of #2,000 to Mr. A was recorded in Mr. B's account. This is an error of _____.
quiz.solution: An error of commission occurs when an entry is made in the correct class of account (Personal) but the wrong individual account (Mr. B instead of Mr. A).

quiz.q: The person who prepares the Petty Cash Book is the _____.
quiz.solution: The petty cashier is a junior staff member responsible for small, daily expenditures.

quiz.q: Unpresented cheques are cheques _____.
options: Drawn but not yet paid by the bank
Rejected by the bank due to errors
quiz.solution: Unpresented cheques have been recorded in the Cash Book (credit side) but have not yet appeared on the Bank Statement.

quiz.q: The Purchases Day Book is used to record _____.
options: Credit purchases of goods for resale
quiz.solution: The Purchases Day Book (or Journal) is specifically for the credit purchase of inventory.

quiz.q: The double entry for 'Cash sales' is _____.
quiz.solution: Cash is increasing (asset debit) and Sales is an income (credit).

quiz.q: Which book of original entry is used to record credit sales of furniture by a company that deals in electronics?
quiz.solution: Sales Journals are for credit sales of trading stock only. Credit sales of non-current assets (furniture) must be recorded in the General Journal (Journal Proper).

quiz.q: The systematic record of all cash and bank transactions is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Cash Book is the primary book of original entry for recording all money received and paid out by the business.

quiz.q: A credit entry in the Sales Account represents _____.
quiz.solution: Sales is an income account. Incomes increase on the credit side and decrease on the debit side.

quiz.q: The book of original entry for credit sales is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Sales Journal.

quiz.q: Which account is used to record small cash payments?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Petty cash book.

quiz.q: Double entry for cash sales:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Dr Cash, Cr Sales.
